_meta.subject: config TLV container: outer CRC, unknown-type skip, chunked CONFIG_WRITE validation
_meta.hex: all frame/reply strings are lowercase hex, even length, no 0x prefix, no spaces
_meta.container: outer packet = [length:2 LE][version:1][single_packet...][crc:2 LE]; single_packet = [number:1][id:1][fixed-size payload] (opendisplay_structs.h:308-322). There is NO per-packet length field: sizeof the struct selected by id IS the payload length.
_meta.crc: toolbox-outer CRC16-CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF) over [length..last packet byte] with the TWO LENGTH BYTES FED AS ZEROS, excluding the trailing CRC field itself (opendisplay_structs.h:289-294; Firmware config_parser.cpp:252-268, NRF54 opendisplay_config_parser.c:70-95, Silabs opendisplay_config_parser.c:17-45). Getting this convention wrong silently invalidates every config vector.
_meta.MAX_CONFIG_SIZE: 4096 on EVERY target as of 2026-07-25 - a global product-wide cap, not a per-target macro (DIVERGENCE 2.7). It is defined per repo (config_parser.h / opendisplay_config_storage.h), NOT in the canonical protocol header. UNRESOLVED: the chunked path cannot actually deliver 4096 bytes. MAX_CONFIG_CHUNKS is 20 (opendisplay_protocol.h:889) and NRF54 handle_config_chunk() rejects once received_chunks >= 20, so the reachable ceiling is 200 + 19*200 = 4000 bytes; a 4001..4096-byte config NACKs mid-transfer despite being within MAX_CONFIG_SIZE. No vector is authored for it because the schema is one frame per vector and demonstrating it needs a 21-frame sequence.
_meta.expect.reply: lowercase hex of the device's reply frame, or null when the device emits no frame
_meta.expect.parsed: SCHEMA EXTENSION (optional). Post-parse assertions the runner checks against the parsed config, for vectors whose real contract is invisible on the reply frame. Keys are dotted paths into the parsed config; absent means 'assert nothing beyond the reply'.
_meta.min_protocol: OD_PROTOCOL_VERSION at which the vector became valid; canonical is 2.2
_meta.requires: OD_*_ENABLE flags that must be ON; [] = unconditional

state.sec_enabled: stored SecurityConfig has encryption_enabled=1 and a non-zero key
state.session: null = no live session; "live" = an authenticated session is open
state.chunk_active: a chunked CONFIG_WRITE started by 0x41 is in progress on this connection
state.chunk_total: declared total_size of the in-progress chunked write
state.chunk_received: bytes accumulated so far in the in-progress chunked write
state.chunk_expected: expected_chunks the device computed at START
state.chunk_count: chunks accepted so far, counting the 0x41 START frame as 1

expect.note: The three @required singletons and nothing else: 0x01 SystemConfig (22 B), 0x02 ManufacturerData (22 B), 0x04 PowerOption (30 B) - opendisplay_structs.h:418,436,484 (@required) and their OD_STATIC_ASSERT sizes at :430,:449,:507. Outer = 3 header + 24 + 24 + 32 + 2 CRC = 85 B, under CONFIG_CHUNK_SIZE (200) so it takes the single-frame CONFIG_WRITE path (opendisplay_protocol.h:316). Ack is the 4-byte config shape (DIVERGENCE 1.4). CAUTION for the Python runner: py-opendisplay 7.14.0 config_parser.py:207-219 ALSO demands a 0x20 display packet and raises ConfigParseError('Missing required packet(s): display') on this blob - the header marks 0x20 @repeatable max=4, not @required (opendisplay_structs.h:688). Host/spec divergence, recorded not resolved.

DIVERGENCE 2.2, the highest-value vector in the corpus. Packet order is 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, then type 0xF0 (in NO size table on any target), then 0x27 SecurityConfig (64 B, opendisplay_structs.h:909-921). Firmware and Silabs force skip-to-CRC on an unrecognised id and therefore LOSE the 0x27 that follows it - the exact bug DIVERGENCE 2.1/2.2 describes, where 0x27 today survives only because it sorts ahead of 0x2A. NRF54 is the model: a size-table skip for known-but-unparsed types plus rescan_security_packet() (opendisplay_config_parser.c:42-64, 621-623) which re-finds a 0x27 after a genuinely unknown id. Assert security is loaded. The 0xF0 payload is 8 bytes of 0xA5; its length is deliberately arbitrary because an unknown type carries no length, which is why recovery needs the rescan and not arithmetic. Key 00..0f is synthetic - never a captured key. CAUTION for the Python runner: py-opendisplay 7.14.0 config_parser.py:127-130 does not skip at all on an unknown type, it BREAKS out of the walk, so it drops 0x27 exactly like the two buggy firmwares.

DIVERGENCE 2.8 - OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR, NOT A DESIRED CONTRACT. Same blob as config_tlv/minimal-required-singletons with both CRC bytes inverted. All three targets treat the toolbox-outer CRC16 as ADVISORY: the mismatch is logged and the config is applied anyway (Firmware config_parser.cpp:665-672, NRF54 opendisplay_config_parser.c:657-670 - which only printf()s 'CRC mismatch', Silabs opendisplay_config_parser.c:490-498). A second, inner CRC32 in the storage record IS enforced on load. Whether shared/core starts ENFORCING the outer CRC16 is an open decision (DIVERGENCE 2.8 resolution column); when it is made, this vector's expectation changes and gains a deprecated_after marker - it must not be read as a licence to keep ignoring the CRC.

Chunked CONFIG_WRITE START. Payload is CONFIG_CHUNK_SIZE_WITH_PREFIX = 202 = total(2 LE) + CONFIG_CHUNK_SIZE(200) (opendisplay_protocol.h:887-888, :316-321). total = 0x0190 = 400, so expected_chunks = 1 + ceil(200/200) = 2 (NRF54 handle_config_write() opendisplay_pipe.c:971-975). The first frame MUST carry a full 200 data bytes: a short first chunk makes firmware take the single-frame path and NACK the following 0x42 chunks (opendisplay_protocol.h:317-319). The 200 data bytes are zero filler - every check on this path is length-only and no TLV parsing happens until the final chunk commits. CAUTION for the Python runner: a 0x41 frame whose payload is 202 bytes is a [total][chunk] START, not a 202-byte config; py-opendisplay's build_write_config_command() takes the whole payload AS the config, so a naive builder round-trip on this vector re-chunks it and mismatches. Such vectors must be skipped host-side, not asserted.

DIVERGENCE 2.3 - declared total > MAX_CONFIG_SIZE is rejected AT START. total = 0x2000 = 8192 > 4096 (MAX_CONFIG_SIZE, global as of 2026-07-25, DIVERGENCE 2.7). NRF54 handle_config_write() opendisplay_pipe.c:930-935 resets the chunk context and sends the 4-byte err[] = {0xFF, RESP_CONFIG_WRITE, 0x00, 0x00}; total == 0 is rejected by the same branch. Firmware does NOT perform this check at all (communication.cpp:456-478) - NRF54 is the model to promote, so this vector is expected to FAIL against an unfixed ESP32 import and that failure is the point. Same Python-runner caveat as config_tlv/chunked-start-valid: this is a chunked START, not a 202-byte config.

DIVERGENCE 2.3 (the connection-binding tightening): a 0x42 CONFIG_CHUNK with no active chunked write - or one bound to a different connection - is NACKed with the 4-byte [0xFF][0x42][0x00][0x00]. NRF54 handle_config_chunk() opendisplay_pipe.c:995-998 (!s_cfg_chunk.active || s_cfg_chunk.connection != connection). opendisplay_protocol.h:330-331.

DIVERGENCE 2.3 - END is rejected when received_size != total_size. Continues config_tlv/chunked-start-valid: 200 of 400 bytes are in, expected_chunks is 2, so this final chunk completes the COUNT (received_chunks >= expected_chunks) while leaving the BYTE total short at 300 != 400. NRF54 handle_config_chunk() opendisplay_pipe.c:1028-1033 resets and NACKs. Firmware commits on the chunk COUNT alone without comparing received_size to total_size (communication.cpp:527-537), so it would ack this and save a 300-byte truncation - the divergence this vector pins.
